content: प्र {%ind.%} .²1 As a prefix to verbs it means ‘forward’, ‘forth’, ‘in front’, ‘onward’, ‘before’, ‘away’, as in प्रगम्, प्रस्था, प्रचर्, प्रया <ab>&c.</ab> .²2 With adjectives it means ‘very’, ‘excessively’, ‘very much’ <ab>&c.</ab>; प्रकृष्ट, प्रमत्त <ab>&c.</ab>, see further on. .²3 With nouns whether derived from verbs or not, it is used in the following senses according to <ls>G. M.</ls>:-- .³({%a%}) beginning, commencement; (प्रयाणम्, प्रस्थानम्, प्राह्ण); .³({%b%}) length (प्रबालभूषिक); .³({%c%}) power (प्रभु); .³({%d%}) intensity, excess (प्रवाद, प्रकर्ष, प्रच्छाय प्रगुण); .³({%e%}) source or origin (प्रभव, प्रपौत्र); .³({%f%}) completion, perfectness, satisfaction (प्रभुक्तमन्नम्); .³({%g%}) destitution, separation, being without (प्रोषिता, प्रपर्णवृक्षः); .³({%h%}) apart (प्रज्ञु); .³({%i%}) excellence (प्राचार्यः); .³({%j%}) purity (प्रसन्नं जलम्); .³({%k%}) wish (प्रार्थना); .³({%l%}) cessation (प्रशम); .³({%m%}) adoration, respect (प्राञ्जलिः who respectfully folds his hands together); .³({%n%}) prominence (प्रणस, प्रवाल). In the Veda it is often used as a separable adverb; <ab>cf.</ab> प्र आदिकर्मदीर्घेशभृशसंभवतृप्तिवियोगशुद्धिशक्तीच्छाशान्तिपूजाग्रदर्शनेषु.
